key_insight: Sea surface roughness and air-sea momentum exchange depend not only on wind speed but also on local wave height and peak frequency, which the paper captures with a scale-invariant subfilter wave drag model in LES.
engineering_relevance: Improved MABL modeling can better support climate prediction, offshore wind design, ocean engineering, and analysis of ocean-atmosphere momentum transfer.
method: Large Eddy Simulation of the marine atmospheric boundary layer over waves
Introduces a local, scale-invariant subfilter wave drag representation
Tests sensitivity to significant wave height and wave spectral peak frequency
evidence_signal: The model outputs are compared against field data and used to examine how momentum flux varies beyond simple monotonic trends with friction velocity and 10 m wind speed.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on subfilter parameterization, its accuracy may depend on how well the local wave statistics and drag closure represent unresolved wave dynamics.
paper_title: Sea Surface Roughness Dependence on Ocean Wave Parameters through Large Eddy Simulation with Local Subfilter Wave Drag
